B001257.text: Juneteenth marks an important moment in our nation's history - the day when the news of emancipation finally reached the last enslaved Americans in Texas, more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was issued.  As we reflect on this day, we honor the resilience, faith, and perseverance of those who endured injustice and helped move our country closer to its founding ideals. We also recognize that America's story is one of continual progress—expanding freedom, protecting opportunity, and striving to build a more perfect Union.  May we always cherish the freedoms we enjoy, learn from our history, and remain committed to the principles of liberty, equality, and justice for all.

I enjoyed the opportunity to tour the Port of Tampa and learn more about the critical role it plays in supporting Florida’s economy, strengthening our supply chain, and creating jobs throughout the region. The Port serves as a vital gateway for commerce and trade, helping connect businesses to domestic and international markets while driving economic growth across our state. I appreciated the chance to meet with Port leaders, hear about their ongoing initiatives, and discuss ways we can continue supporting the infrastructure and investments needed to keep Florida’s economy moving forward. #PortTampaBay #EconomicGrowth #Infrastructure #FloridaJobs

I was honored to welcome leaders from the Tampa Bay area to Washington, D.C., and escort them to the National Archives, where they had the unique opportunity to view some of America's most treasured founding documents and experience firsthand the history that continues to shape our country today.  There is nothing quite like standing before the documents that enshrine our freedoms and reflect the principles upon which our Nation was built. Moments like these serve as a powerful reminder of the responsibilities we share as citizens and leaders to preserve and strengthen the American experiment for future generations.  If you are planning a trip to our Nation's Capital, I encourage you to contact my office at least 90 days in advance. My team is always happy to assist constituents in arranging tours of some of Washington's most iconic sites, including the U.S. Capitol, the White House, the National Archives, and other historic landmarks. We would be honored to help make your visit a memorable one!

I appreciated the opportunity to stand alongside my friend and tireless advocate, Gary Dassatti, in support of the fight against ALS. Gary's dedication to keeping Doug’s memory alive through advocacy and awareness is truly inspiring. Together, we remain committed to supporting groundbreaking research, raising awareness, and bringing hope to the patients and families affected by ALS as we work toward the ultimate goal of finding a cure.

I was proud to help honor the 877 exceptional young people from across our Nation who have earned the Congressional Award Gold Medal—the highest honor Congress bestows upon youth for achievement in voluntary public service, personal development, physical fitness, and exploration.  These outstanding awardees traveled to the U.S. Capitol to meet with Members of Congress, engage with business and civic leaders, and participate in discussions with experts on topics ranging from STEM education and financial empowerment to travel and exploration.  Each of these Gold Medal recipients has demonstrated extraordinary dedication, perseverance, and a commitment to serving others. They have challenged themselves, set ambitious goals, and made meaningful contributions to their communities, proving that the future of our country is in very capable hands.  I was especially honored to serve as a panelist for the Travel and Exploration discussion, where we explored how experiencing new places, cultures, and perspectives can broaden horizons, build confidence, and inspire future leaders. Travel has a unique ability to foster curiosity, resilience, and a deeper understanding of the world around us.Congratulations to all of this year's Congressional Award Gold Medalists. Your hard work, character, and spirit of service embody the very best of America, and I look forward to seeing all that you accomplish in the years ahead.

Terrorists. Cartels. Human traffickers. Drug smugglers. Each day, ICE and Border Patrol agents and officers confront these threats head-on to keep America safe. It’s exactly why I have consistently voted to comprehensively resource these law enforcement professionals as they carry out their security missions. While the far-left hoped to eradicate funding for critical operations and weaken our border security apparatus, House Republicans have made clear that we will continue to support those who defend our homeland and keep our communities safe. That's why we passed the Secure America Act today.

However, while I do not regret the objective of our actions today, I am appalled by the complete failure of Senate Democrats that led us to this moment. Chuck Schumer and his radical caucus twice shut down the government, instigating chaos across the nation. Since then, they have continued to diminish Article I and forced the use of reconciliation. It’s wrong – and deliberately undermines the appropriations process.

The Constitution entrusts Congress with the power of the purse. Yet, in great irony, the Senate has shown greater concern for protecting an internal rule than fulfilling its constitutional duty. The filibuster is nothing more than an institutional habit. It is neither mentioned nor sanctioned in our founding documents. I would remind my peers on the other side of the Rotunda that no chamber precedent is greater than the bedrock of our Republic. Members swear an oath to uphold the Constitution – not the filibuster.

I thoroughly regret the erosion of Article I authority that Senate Democrats have instigated, and the price everyday Americans have been forced to pay as a result. I hope the months-long charade that led us to this moment serves as a reminder that no partisan fixation is worth shutting down the government, abandoning constitutional responsibilities, and forcing Congress into extraordinary measures simply to perform its most basic duties.

I believe in the Constitution, the power of the purse, and completing the appropriations process. I also believe in keeping the homeland safe. The Senate may have abandoned proper governing, but I will not abandon those who stand watch over our borders and protect our communities.

Our work, of course, doesn’t end here. As the Fiscal Year 2027 Appropriations markups near completion, I am reminded that governing is a choice. The work I do, the votes I cast, and the actions I take will always be guided by one principle: fulfilling our obligations to the American people

For 39 years, Governor Bill Anoatubby has led my tribe, the Chickasaw Nation, with remarkable vision, a strategic hand, and unwavering dedication. His leadership has transformed not only the trajectory of the Nation, but the lives of the Chickasaw people.
 
Economically, his tenure has been nothing short of historic and unprecedented. Through Governor Anoatubby’s steady leadership, the Chickasaw Nation did more than just achieve its goals of economic development and self-sufficiency – it surpassed them. Under his guidance, the tribe evolved from dependence on federal funding to one that is self-sufficient and prosperous on its own. Today, thanks to him, the Chickasaw Nation supports more than 22,000 jobs and contributes $3.7 billion annually to Oklahoma’s economy, including $1.2 billion in wages and benefits.
 
However, Governor Anoatubby’s impact cannot be measured by just economics. Throughout his lengthy tenure, he also placed a significant emphasis on preserving and sharing the precious heritage of the Chickasaw Nation. Through initiatives such as the Chickasaw Nation Division of Arts and Humanities and the Chickasaw Cultural Center, he ensured that our history, language, arts, and culture would continue to inspire future generations.
 
These achievements, on top of many others, make it unmistakably clear: Governor Bill Anoatubby is the most consequential Chickasaw Nation leader since the removal period. And his influence has extended past just the Chickasaw Nation. His leadership and impact are respected by every Oklahoman.
 
For nearly four decades, Governor Anoatubby has embodied true commitment to the Chickasaw people and Oklahoma. The powerful combination of his leadership, vision, and generosity has allowed all of us in our state to shape a brighter future for ourselves and all those touched by the results of his leadership. On a personal level, I am fortunate to call Governor Anoatubby a mentor and a trusted friend.
 
His retirement is an enormous loss for the Chickasaw Nation, all Indian Country, and the state of Oklahoma. However, he leaves the tribe stronger than he found it, as he hands it off to his very competent and bright son, Chris, the Lieutenant Governor. I have no doubt Chris will carry on his father’s legacy with wisdom, competence, and care, and I look forward to seeing everything the future holds for the Chickasaw Nation.
 
In conclusion, to Governor Anoatubby, congratulations on a truly remarkable career and a lifetime of service. Thank you for your leadership, your vision, your friendship, and the legacy you leave behind. I wish you, Janice, and your entire family the best as you enter this next chapter.

This morning, I joined City of Laredo Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño and State Representative Richard Raymond to discuss the growing threat of the New World screwworm and the ongoing efforts at the federal, state, and local levels to protect livestock, animal health, and our agricultural economy.

We know how to beat this pest because we've done it before. That's why I've been pushing for increased sterile fly production, stronger USDA resources, and additional support for ranchers and producers. I urged the USDA to establish a domestic sterile fly production facility, supported efforts to provide $300 million for domestic sterile fly production capacity, and secured House Appropriations Committee language directing APHIS to make a domestic facility a priority. Just this week, the USDA also announced approximately $105 million for 40 new research projects focused on combating the screwworm and other livestock threats, with Texas institutions playing a leading role.

For pet owners looking for more information, my office put together a handout on New World screwworm treatments for pets, including signs to watch for and available treatment options: https://cuellar.house.gov/UploadedFiles/New_World_Screwworm_Treatment_for_Petss.docx.pdf

I appreciate Mayor Treviño, Representative Raymond, and all our local, state, and federal partners for helping raise awareness and keep South Texas informed.

We'll continue working together to protect our communities, support our ranching families, and ensure we're prepared to stop this threat before it spreads.

Yesterday, I joined Commissioner Chad McIntosh, State Representative Richard Raymond, Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño, local leaders, and partners for the signing ceremony marking a major milestone in the proposed expansion of the World Trade Bridge. I asked Commissioner McIntosh to come to Laredo for this important occasion, and I appreciate him being here to sign this agreement in person with our community.

With the U.S. International Boundary and Water Commission’s approval of the binational joint review, the project can now move forward toward expanding capacity at one of the nation’s busiest trade crossings. The expansion will help reduce congestion, improve commercial traffic flow, and strengthen the supply chains that support jobs and economic growth across South Texas and the country.

As a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, I’ll continue working with our local, state, and federal partners to help move this project forward and ensure Laredo remains a leader in international trade.

This is an important step forward for Laredo, South Texas, and the future of U.S.-Mexico trade.

I joined community leaders and partners to celebrate the inauguration of GXO’s new warehouse and logistics facility.

As a global leader in logistics and supply chain solutions, GXO’s investment reinforces Laredo’s role as a key hub for international trade and economic growth. Facilities like this help strengthen supply chains, support businesses, and create new opportunities across our region.

This investment reflects the strong partnerships that continue driving growth in South Texas. Congratulations to GXO and everyone who helped make this project possible. I look forward to seeing the positive impact it will have on our community!

Ensuring a reliable water supply is critical to Laredo’s future growth and success.

At the Laredo Water Museum, I joined Mayor Dr. Victor Treviño, City Councilmembers, State Representative Richard Raymond, and JasperRuth Ranch Water Operating LLC to recognize Laredo’s first ever secondary water source agreement, an important step toward strengthening the city’s long term water reliability.

As Laredo continues to grow, diversifying our water supply will help support future demand, economic development, and resilience for years to come. I’ll continue working to support investments that strengthen water infrastructure across South Texas.

Congratulations to the City of Laredo and everyone who helped make this agreement possible.

Many of our rural towns and villages rely on diesel generation to keep their lights on, homes warm, and to power four-wheelers and skiffs for subsistence hunting and fishing. 

These communities already faced some of the highest energy costs in the country, but those prices have now risen even further—often to $10 a gallon or more—and have been locked in for months, sometimes longer, because they only receive fuel shipments once or twice a year when sea ice has receded. 

We have a responsibility to help. Congress can complement the state's efforts and ensure that those who face the toughest burdens from higher energy costs in Alaska and around the nation have the support they need to make it through this difficult time.

For the past decade, the Ocean Observatories Initiative has generated publicly available, real-time data that provides crucial insights into changing ecosystem conditions and extreme weather. The loss of this deep-water observation system would leave public safety officials, natural disaster responders, coastal communities, fishermen, and other industries without the vital information they need. I urge the National Science Foundation to abide by congressional intent and legal direction, which clearly require maintaining the operation of this cost-effective research system.

Today we honor the life and legacy of Gilbert “Butch” Wallace, a devoted husband, father, grandfather, friend, and public servant whose impact on our community will be felt for generations. 

Butch is survived by his beloved wife of 48 years, Carolyn Wallace, their two daughters, Heather Wallace and Michelle Boone, and grandson Tyler Muller. Together they built a family grounded in faith, service, and love.

The Wilson family always welcomed him as “Uncle Butch,” Attorney General Alan Wilson and Palmetto State Armory founder Julian Wilson were especially encouraged by “Uncle Butch.”

A Florida native, Butch attended Florida State University where he earned a degree in Communications and Business. He went on to build a successful State Farm Agency, serving his community for 48 years. Through his work, he not only helped countless families and businesses, butalso, created jobs and contributed to the economic growth of our state. 

For more than 20 years, Butch has served as avalued member of my staff, where he touched the lives of countless South Carolinians, including my own. His wisdom and unwavering commitment to others made him an indispensable member of Team Wilson and a trusted friend of all those who worked alongside him. 
His dedication to service extended far beyond his professional life. He was deeply involved in his community serving as a Charter Member and President of the West Metro Rotary Club, President of the National Kidney Foundation of South Carolina, a member of the National Federation of Independent Business State Advisory Council, and a member of the Boy Scouts of America Indian Waters Council Board.   

Additionally, in 2019, he was a recipient of the Order of the Palmetto, South Carolina’s highest civilian award. 
His commitment to civic engagement led him to serve in many political leadership roles including as Chairman of the Lexington County Republican Party and as a delegate to many state and county conventions. 

Butch lived a life defined by service, integrity, and kindness. South Carolina is better because of his contributions, and all who knew him are better for having called him a friend. He leaves behind a legacy of leadership, compassion, and service that will endure long beyond his lifetime.

May we honor Butch by striving to serve others with the same dedication and grace that he demonstrated throughout his remarkable life.

This morning at Historic Boone Farm in Middletown Township, on Juneteenth, our community witnessed something truly special: a dream realized.

The African American Museum of Bucks County now has a home worthy of the history it preserves, the stories it carries, and the generations it will teach.

On a day that reminds us freedom must be taught, protected, and remembered, this museum gives our community a permanent place to do that sacred work.

This day belongs to my dear friend, the late Linda Salley. For years, Linda carried these stories across our community—into schools, churches, libraries, and gathering places—because she knew Bucks County’s African American history deserved to be known, honored, and passed on.

She was right.

Working alongside Linda and the AAMBC team to bring this vision to life has been one of the great honors of my service, including securing $2 million to help complete the restoration and expansion of Boone Farm.

Linda and I shared a deep belief that this history deserved more than a temporary home. It deserved permanence. It deserved a place to stand. And today, because of her vision and the dedication of so many, it has one.

The story of Bucks County cannot be fully told without the stories this museum preserves. And because of Linda’s faith, leadership, and love for this community, those stories will continue to teach, inspire, and endure for generations.

Congratulations to the entire AAMBC team, board, staff, volunteers, partners, and every person who made this possible—and my sincere thanks to my incredible friend, Pastor Don Schuler, for providing such special remarks on my behalf.

On June 19, 1865, more than two years after the Emancipation Proclamation, Union troops arrived in Galveston, Texas, to announce and enforce emancipation—a turning point in our nation’s long march toward justice.

For those who had been denied the truth of their freedom, Juneteenth marked a long-overdue day of liberation. For our nation, it remains a defining moment in America’s ongoing journey toward justice, equality, and human dignity.

That is why, in 2021, I helped lead the effort to establish Juneteenth as a federal holiday—to honor this historic moment, preserve its rightful place in our national memory, and recognize the generations of Americans whose courage, faith, perseverance, and sacrifice have carried our country closer to its founding ideals.

As Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. reminded us, “Injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere.” Today, we honor this legacy by reflecting on that truth and renewing our commitment to justice, equality, freedom, and dignity for all.

Great to join our friends at St. Gregorios Malankara Orthodox Church in Bensalem to mark 50 years of fellowship, service, and faith in action.

A parish is built by people—by parents and grandparents, by clergy and volunteers, by children raised in tradition, and by families who choose, year after year, to show up for one another. That is the legacy St. Gregorios shares with all of our PA-1 faith communities: neighbors helping neighbors, families strengthening families, and traditions enriching the diverse fabric of our community.

Congratulations to Rev. Fr. Shibu V. Mathai and the entire St. Gregorios family!

On June 14, 1777, our young nation adopted a flag not just as a symbol, but as a statement: that liberty, unity, sacrifice, and service would define who we are as Americans.

As we prepare to celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, Flag Day carries an even deeper meaning. It reminds us of the generations of brave men and women who have defended our flag and the shared responsibility we have to carry its promise forward.

This morning, I was honored to join our friends from the Fairless Hills Elks Lodge #2023 for their annual Flag Day ceremony, a proud Bucks County tradition that keeps that spirit alive. The Elks have been stewards of patriotism and service since 1868, and I have long been grateful for their partnership in honoring our history, supporting our veterans, and investing in the next generation of leaders.

Thank you to Lodge #2023 for all you do for our community, and for making this annual tradition such a meaningful reminder of what it means to be an American.

Join me in congratulating Aiden Ertwine of Warrington, Magnus Figueroa of Holicong, Kian Wilson of Pipersville, and Mitav Mehta of Furlong, all of Troop 71, on earning the rank of Eagle Scout!

Each of these young men completed a meaningful service project rooted in stewardship, conservation, and care for the natural world around us.

For his project, Mitav built an 85-foot boardwalk at Heritage Conservancy’s Jackson Pond Nature Preserve, helping protect sensitive habitats by reducing erosion from runoff while providing visitors with a safe, elevated pathway to experience the preserve.

Magnus also partnered with Heritage Conservancy, creating an informational kiosk for one of its preserved properties and replacing a drainage pipe to help improve the site for future visitors.

At Aark Wildlife Rehabilitation and Education Center, Aiden created a mammal enclosure for rabies-vector mammals in need of rehabilitation, while Kian built a new enclosure to provide mammals and rodents with a safe sanctuary as they recover and receive care.

Together, these projects reflect the very best of Scouting: seeing a need, stepping forward, and using leadership and hard work to strengthen the places, organizations, and natural resources that make our community so special.

Congratulations to each of you—and thank you to your families, Scout leaders, Troop 71, and the entire PA-1 Scouting community for continuing to lead through service.

RT by @RepMikeLevin: The White House finally sent members of Congress the new Iran deal. It didn’t take very long to read. In short, I think it’s a joke. It hands Iran everything and gets almost nothing back.
 
Compare it to the 2015 nuclear deal Trump tore up. That agreement forced Iran to ship 97% of its enriched uranium out of the country, rip out two thirds of its centrifuges, and accept the toughest inspections ever placed on any nation, all while leaving in place non-nuclear sanctions against the regime. It was not perfect. But it bought verified distance from a bomb.
 
This new deal does the opposite. It allows Iran to stay exactly where it stands today, after years of secret progress that nearly created enough uranium for 10 nuclear bombs. The hard nuclear questions get pushed to talks that may never happen.
 
And look at what America gives up front. We immediately waive sanctions on Iranian energy exports that fund the regime. We release roughly $24 billion in frozen assets. We even promise to organize at least $300 billion to rebuild Iran and lift every single U.S. sanction. In return, Iran promises to negotiate later.
 
Missiles, human rights, and Iran’s terror proxies were dropped from the agenda entirely.
 
I will always support diplomacy over a war that Americans never asked for. But a deal the enemy is celebrating tells you all you need to know about who came out on top.
 
This agreement leaves America and its allies weaker. Senator Cassidy was spot on when he said yesterday that Reagan is rolling over in his grave.

“Habeas Corpus.” It’s a complicated term for a simple idea: the government can’t keep you locked up without giving you a chance to challenge it in front of a judge.

New reporting reveals that the Trump Administration seriously debated taking that right away from immigrants, so they could be detained and deported without ever getting the chance to challenge it in court. Even some of Trump’s own lawyers warned that doing this would be unconstitutional. 
 
This should scare you regardless of your politics. Once a president decides he can detain people without letting them challenge it before a judge, what’s stopping him from deciding who else that applies to next? 
 
Governments that can lock people up and remove them from the country without any judge ever weighing in aren’t democracies anymore. That’s textbook authoritarianism.

Fun Fact Friday: As we celebrate the 250th anniversary of American independence, I want to highlight some of the signers of the Declaration of Independence.
Lewis Morris was born in New York in 1726 and graduated from Yale in 1742. Lewis, who lived among loyalists in the upper class section of New York, was originally loyal to Britain. He grew frustrated with British trading policy and when he was elected to serve in the Continental Congress, he worked to lobby the state of New York towards independence. He also worked with local Native American groups to ensure their neutrality or their support of independence. On July 9th, 1776, New York voted for independence, making the vote for independence unanimous on July 11, 1776. Morris returned to New York where he served as Judge of Westchester County, member of the Committee on Detection of Conspiracies, as a Senator in New York, and in the Westchester County Militia, where he rose to the rank of Major General. He was a member of New York’s first Board of Regents of the University of New York and served as a delegate to the State Convention that ratified the Federal Constitution in 1788.

Our team was honored to attend the opening of “From Criollo to Cracker: Florida Cow Culture, an American Story,” a fascinating exhibit highlighting the deep roots of Florida’s cattle industry and the ranching traditions that helped shape our state.

Long before Florida became known for its beaches and tourism, cattle ranching was a way of life across much of what is now Florida’s 18th Congressional District. From Polk County’s working ranches to the historic cattle drives that helped build local communities, agriculture remains an important part of our heritage and economy.

A special thank you to Polk County Clerk of Courts Stacy M. Butterfield and her team for preserving and restoring the Historic Cattle Brand Books, which document more than 160 years of ranching history. These remarkable records, dating from approximately 1862 to 1945, offer a unique glimpse into the families, ranches, and traditions that helped build Florida. You can explore the records online at https://kofilequicklinks.com/PolkFL/.

As we celebrate America250, exhibits like this remind us that the story of Florida ranching is truly an American story, one of hard work, perseverance, innovation, and a deep connection to the land.

As America approaches its 250th anniversary, one thing is strikingly clear: the American experiment is alive and stronger than ever.

President George Washington forged a nation from the ashes of revolution. From leading the Continental Army through the brutal winter at Valley Forge to securing victory at Yorktown, his courage and resolve helped deliver American independence.

But perhaps Washington’s greatest act of leadership came after victory. He willingly laid down power, rejecting the tyranny and permanence of monarchy that defined the old world. In doing so, he established the standard for constitutional government and the transfer of power that still defines our Republic today.

In his farewell address, Washington warned Americans about political division and the dangers of factions. More than 250 years later, his words still ring true.

The legacy of George Washington lives on in every American who believes in freedom, self-government, and the enduring promise of this nation.

Now, after 5 months of seeking a way out of the mess he created, President Trump presents us with a “deal,” which grants Iran access to a $300 billion reconstruction fund, provides immediate sanctions relief for the IRGC and its terrorist proxies, and does nothing to quell Iran's nuclear ambitions.  It may also result in Iran imposing a maritime fee on oil transported through the Straits of Hormuz, an international waterway, putting a higher price tag on oil passed off on consumers.  Worst of all, Iran’s ballistic missile and drone programs remain untouched, leaving America and our allies as exposed as ever to the Iranian regime.  

I see no art in this deal. President Trump has clearly missed the mark in achieving a result that benefits the American people. This agreement must be fully vetted by Congress with all relevant officials involved facing tough questioning; they must make the case for why they think this deal is merited. It is, on the surface, a very poor result.

Today, the Protect College Sports Act advanced out of Senate committee on a strong bipartisan 19–9 vote — a big step toward bringing fairness, stability, and common sense back to college sports.

Cantwell have put together a serious bipartisan bill that puts student-athletes first — all 500,000 of them — with clear rules, real protections, a responsible path for revenue sharing with students and between shcools; stronger NIL protections; and needed guardrails on the transfer portal.

WORLD_INDIA_PM.text:
পশ্চিমবঙ্গ দিবস উপলক্ষে পশ্চিমবঙ্গের আমার  বোন ও ভাইদের জানাই আন্তরিক শুভেচ্ছা।

এই দিনটি এমন এক রাজ্যকে উদযাপন করে যা সাহিত্য, সঙ্গীত, শিল্প, আধ্যাত্মিকতা, বিজ্ঞান, বাণিজ্য ও ব্যবসা, সমাজ সংস্কার এবং আরও অনেক বৈচিত্র্যময় ক্ষেত্রে তার অবদানের মাধ্যমে ভারতের ইতিহাসকে রূপদান করেছে। বারবার, অগণিত  ভাবে পশ্চিমবঙ্গ  ভারতের জাতীয় চেতনাকে সমৃদ্ধ করেছে।

পশ্চিমবঙ্গের ইতিহাসে ২০ জুন দিনটি অত্যন্ত তাৎপর্যপূর্ণ। এই দিনেই নিশ্চিত করা হয়েছিল যে পশ্চিমবঙ্গ ভারতের একটি অংশ হিসেবেই থাকবে। এর পেছনে ছিল ড. শ্যামাপ্রসাদ মুখার্জীর অমূল্য অবদান।  ২০২৬ সালে, আমরা ড. মুখার্জীর ১২৫তম জন্মজয়ন্তীও পালন করছি।

জনগণের স্বপ্ন ও আকাঙ্ক্ষা পূরণের জন্য কেন্দ্রীয় সরকার পশ্চিমবঙ্গ সরকারের সঙ্গে যৌথভাবে কাজ করবে। আমি পশ্চিমবঙ্গের অগ্রগতি এবং পশ্চিমবঙ্গবাসীর সমৃদ্ধির জন্য প্রার্থনা করছি।

Warm greetings to my sisters and brothers of West Bengal on the occasion of Paschimbanga Divas.

This day celebrates a state that has profoundly shaped India's history through its contributions to diverse areas be it literature, music, art, spirituality, science, trade and commerce, social reform and more. Time and again, West Bengal has enriched India's national consciousness in countless ways.

Today, 20th June is of immense significance in West Bengal’s history. This was the day which ensured that West Bengal remains an integral part of India. The role of Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee was invaluable in the same. This year, 2026, we are also marking the 125th Jayanti of Dr. Mookerjee. 

The Central Government will work with the West Bengal Government to fulfil the dreams and aspirations of the people. I pray for the progress of West Bengal and the prosperity of its people.

Warm birthday greetings to the President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu Ji. Her journey, marked by courage, simplicity, humility and unwavering commitment to public service, continues to inspire people across the country. 

Through her many years in public life, she has served the nation in an outstanding manner, especially passionate about the wellbeing of the underprivileged and marginalised. Her steadfast dedication to India’s development is very motivating. 

May she be blessed with a long and healthy life in the service of the nation. I look forward to meeting her later today at the programme in Odisha.
